stdout: usage: bale relay [-h] sid [file]
The exchange thread's recording verb (ADR-0017, v0.4.18). Ingests one exchange
from either side — a clarification manifest, an exchange record, or the BALE
EXCHANGE paste block wrapping either — verifies a block's sha256 trailer
against its body before trusting it, validates the record (exchange-
record.schema.json; the question rows by reference to response-
manifest.schema.json), refuses a session_id other than <sid>, a round that is
not the thread's next NNN, a planner record as round one, or an answer that
does not resolve to a preserved question, then preserves the record as the
next NNN under .bale/clarifications/<sid>/ (the same write apply's
clarification ingest uses), retains the lock — the session stays suspended —
and emits the counterpart-facing paste block on stdout with every [bale] line
on stderr. Direction is read from the record's `from`, never from a flag.
Executes nothing and stages nothing. With no file argument (v0.4.22), re-emits
the paste block for the thread's latest recorded round, byte-identical to the
original emission, and records nothing; a sid with no recorded rounds refuses
loudly.
positional arguments:
sid         The suspended session's id (full form YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>-NNN).
Must be open in the registry with no bale/<sid> branch; the
record's session_id must match.
file        Path to the exchange — an exchange record, a clarification
manifest, or the paste block wrapping either — or `-` to read it
from stdin. A relative path resolves like apply's tarball
argument: cwd first, then each configured apply.search_paths
directory; an absolute path bypasses the search. CRLF line
endings are normalized at read. Omitted entirely, the no-file
form re-emits the paste block for the thread's latest recorded
round, byte-identical to the original emission, and records
nothing (v0.4.22).
options:
-h, --help  show this help message and exit
